approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including an aromatic nitrogen/carbon exchange that preserves molecular formula. After normalizing identities and rejecting duplicates, it submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local motif changes. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move worsens the current score, using canonical text order for exact score ties. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, choose the one whose local motif counts differ most from the current molecule, then use canonical order if that structural comparison also ties. The distance accounts for motif multiplicity and normalizes by the combined motif counts. This gives an equally scored change in local chemical environments priority over canonical spelling and may expose a different next neighborhood. The earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms; this rule can choose smaller, equal-sized or larger graphs. It reuses the Parent's existing motifs without changing the generation or tabu rules and adds no history policy.

hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with greatest multiset-Jaccard distance between its inherited radius-one motif occurrence counts and the current source's counts, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.

finding_summary.headline: Motif-distance ties changed 20 walk states, but the panel score fell
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out failure to exercise the selector: it changed real, scored next states and was followed by 600 later accepted proposals after removing overlap between the recorded histories. It also shows why larger local structural steps are insufficient evidence of more useful exploration. The extra plateau profiles came with extra plateau moves, and longer equal-score episodes still appeared. Twenty later archive gains occurred in the affected continuations, compared with 26 in the corresponding recorded parent histories, but the overlapping paths prevent assigning a causal gain to each tie choice. The rule sometimes chose smaller molecules and sometimes larger ones. The molecular assessment finds that some equally scored differences introduce reactive attachments or unusual sulfur connectivity, while conventional ring and carbonyl families remain available. Greater distance between local motif counts therefore supplies neither compactness nor chemical plausibility. The direct selection mechanism is confirmed; its proposed overall score benefit is refuted on this panel. What remains open is whether a distance that distinguishes useful structural alternatives from score-insensitive local decoration can improve later search; this experiment does not settle that broader question.
finding_summary.results: Twenty choices among equally best accepted molecules changed the next walk state, and all 20 increased exact motif distance from the current molecule without giving up the accepted maximum score. Eighteen occurred at the same score as the source, one during an improving move and one during a worsening move. Nineteen choices had actual continuations; one was terminal. The rule encountered 40 exact maximum ties, compared with 26 in the parent, while preserving canonical fallback and the original feedback, archive and memory rules. Plateau episodes contained 60 equal-score moves, each visiting a distinct motif profile within its episode, compared with 49 such moves in the parent. Coverage per move was unchanged, and the longest plateau grew from six moves to nine. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519947, a paired loss of 0.001812 against the required gain of 0.002. One seed improved slightly and two declined. Only deco_hop endpoints changed; the other four task endpoints were identical in every seed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl/carbonyl families coexist with reactive attachments, oversized decorations and undefined sulfur cages
molecular.overall_character: Node n-4341f3da1e57 was assessed from all supplied trajectories for all five tasks and all three seeds; the digest has no tasks_without_trajectories. Each task contains 900 evaluated records, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposals are branched, ring-rich molecules: every task has string-level ring_closure_rate 1.0, while aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0. These are presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Charged and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0 throughout. The chemical range includes comparatively conventional fused aromatic amides, decorated oxo/thioxo azaheterocycles, aryl compounds carrying primary and cyclic amines, bridged N/O lactams, and densely connected fluorinated sulfur cages. Diversity is moderate across these families but the displayed leaders repeatedly vary the same local frameworks. Rings, aromatic groups, carbonyls and amines are already accessible. The recurring deficiencies are stable heteroatom connectivity, economical substitution, and defined feasible stereochemistry. Many leading sulfur-rich graphs have weak synthetic credibility, although some indole amides have recognizable conventional chemistry. Passive parsing with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6 environment succeeded for every supplied child and parent trajectory molecule. All atom, ring and functional-bond counts below are derived directly from those observed graphs; ring counts use toolkit perception and do not certify geometry or synthesis. The passive descriptors, input hashes and comparison receipts are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-06-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json, produced by the adjacent molecular-audit.py. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, every replica retains the same best molecular identity set on four tasks. The changed best identities are confined to deco_hop, whose chemistry is described below. method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out failure to exercise the selector: it changed real, scored next states and was followed by 600 later accepted proposals after removing overlap between the recorded histories. The extra plateau profiles came with extra plateau moves, and longer equal-score episodes still appeared. Greater distance between local motif counts therefore supplies neither compactness nor chemical plausibility. The direct selection mechanism is confirmed; its proposed overall score benefit is refuted on this panel. What remains open is whether a distance that distinguishes useful structural alternatives from score-insensitive local decoration can improve later search; this experiment does not settle that broader question.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including an aromatic nitrogen/carbon exchange that preserves molecular formula. After normalizing identities and rejecting duplicates, it submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local motif changes. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move worsens the current score, using canonical text order for exact score ties. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, choose the one whose local motif counts differ most from the current molecule, then use canonical order if that structural comparison also ties. The distance accounts for motif multiplicity and normalizes by the combined motif counts. This gives an equally scored change in local chemical environments priority over canonical spelling and may expose a different next neighborhood. The earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms; this rule can choose smaller, equal-sized or larger graphs. It reuses the Parent's existing motifs without changing the generation or tabu rules and adds no history policy.
